header.title_en: Grade 5 · English · FDE pattern practice paper
header.title_ur: جماعت پنجم · انگریزی · FDE pattern کا مشقی پرچہ
header.note_en: Note: This paper consists of THREE Sections. Section – A needs to be solved on the Question Paper. Sections B & C are to be solved on the Answer Sheet. Cutting, erasing and overwriting is not allowed.

slots.instruction_en: Read each question carefully and choose the correct option. Each question carries 1 mark.

grain.kind: one grammar or vocabulary point per item

slots.prompt_rule: Twenty four-option MCQs, one point each, covering: collective and proper nouns, articles, irregular plurals, antonyms, pronouns, syllables, adverbs, suffixes, tenses, homophones, compound words, degrees of adjectives, modals, apostrophe, spelling, anagrams, sentence types, quantifiers, adjectives. Never refer to an underline the paper cannot show; quote the word instead. An antonym item has one exact opposite among its options. Each stem is one grammatical question with exactly one true option: two options that are both correct (should and could both give advice) is a fault, so a modal item names the one meaning only that modal has. The right answer is never the longest option and never repeats a word of its stem. A stem never prints a word that another question asks the child to find or use (a word-box word, an exclamation mark, a tense name). Ask for a tense change at most twice on the whole paper, counting this question and Q1 (b) and Q2.

grain.kind: one-line transformation: rewrite as a simile, identify subject + verb + object, change the tense, simile or metaphor

slots.prompt_rule: Five one-line items, each ending with the direction in round brackets, e.g. "The baby is sleeping. (Change into simple past)". Cover similes/metaphors, S+V+O and simple present/past. At most two of the five items ask for a tense change, and each item tests a different tense or form: never two items with the same direction (v37 i and v both said "Change into simple past"). Every simile or metaphor item (the child writes the sentence) carries `scheme.accept`, an accept line of at least two different correct rewrites (for "as fast as a cheetah" also "as fast as the wind"), because many sentences are right (v35 Q1(b) i-iii had one model and no accept line).

slots.instruction_en: Read the following passage and answer the questions given at the end.

parts_spec.label: iii.
parts_spec.instruction_en: Choose three nouns and three verbs from the given passage.

grain.kind: an unseen narrative passage of about 120 words; five literal or inference questions; four do-as-directed items tied to the passage; three nouns and three verbs

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `passage` = an unseen story of 120–160 words; `parts` = [{key:"questions", questions:[5]}, {key:"do_as_directed", questions:[4: a part of speech of a quoted word, a tense change, a fill-in from the passage, a true/false]}, {key:"pick", pick:{"Nouns":[5 nouns], "Verbs":[5 verbs]}}]. Every picked word is copied exactly as written in the passage, inflection included ("walked", never "walk"); two spares of each kind, the scheme keeps the first three that are in the passage. Never refer to an underlined, bold or italic word; quote the word instead (What part of speech is "quickly"?). A tense rewrite's `accept` never holds another tense. A true/false item never restates the fact a part i question asks (v35: i(c) asked why Maya ran to the shop and ii(d) said she went to buy a rope); it tests a different sentence of the passage. A False statement is contradicted by a sentence the passage states, never one the passage merely leaves out; a True statement repeats a stated fact in other words. A "why do you think" item asks for a reason the passage does not state; when the passage states the reason, ask it as a plain "why" and every point can be earned by copying the passage, with no second point for an extra reason (v35 i(b)). Each model answer answers the question as asked, from the passage: re-read each model answer against its question before returning it (v37 i(e) asked about being on time and the key said "carry one bucket at a time"). The passage shares no theme or events with the Q9 story outline: it is not about an animal helped by a child and carries no kindness moral, so the writing task cannot be copied from it. Part i: when a scheme pays "Answers in a complete sentence", the stem says "Answer in complete sentences." and every accept line is a full sentence, never a fragment; otherwise the scheme pays content only.

grain.kind: one or two sentences (about 25 words) with capitals, full stops, a question or exclamation mark, commas and an apostrophe removed

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = the unpunctuated passage (lower case, no punctuation), `answer` = the punctuated passage: the printed words exactly, only capitals and punctuation added, nothing reworded, added or dropped; never turn a reported question into direct speech. A points only, one per mark, each for punctuation the printed words can carry (a question mark only where the printed words ask a direct question). No point pays a mark already printed in `question`: the printed passage keeps any apostrophe it shows, so no point is for that apostrophe (v35: "it's" was printed and paid). An end-mark point never needs one particular mark where two are right: it accepts a full stop or an exclamation mark after a statement, and asks for a question mark only after the direct question.

slots.instruction_en: Use any five of the following words in meaningful sentences.

grain.kind: six unit vocabulary words, any five used in sentences

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `words` = exactly six words from units 1–10; `answer` = one model sentence per word, no definitions. 2 marks a word: the sentence shows what the word means 1 + the sentence is correct 1. The paper asks only for sentences, so never ask for, or mark, a written meaning.

slots.instruction_en: Write down FOUR rhyming words from the poem “{q}”

grain.kind: match four cue words to their rhymes in a 9–10 line poem from the book

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = the title of a poem from units 1–10 exactly as in the book; `passage` = 6–10 of its lines exactly as printed in the book, holding at least two rhyming pairs; no `words` (the four rhyming words are the answer, so nothing on the paper may list them); `answer` = the four rhyming words as two pairs, each word copied from the passage (e.g. "white – night; wet – yet").

grain.kind: a textbook topic; the child draws a map with five branches

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = a short topic from units 1–10 (2–4 words). The child draws the map; never refer to boxes or branches printed on the paper. `answer` = five possible branches.

grain.kind: a formal application OR an informal letter from FDE's closed lists

slots.prompt_rule: Two items: (a) "Write an application to your principal for …" with a topic from closed_lists.applications; (b) "Write a letter …" with a topic from closed_lists.informal_letters. The paper sets no length, so the key awards no mark for length and states no sentence or word count.

slots.instruction_en: Write a paragraph on any ONE of the following topics.

grain.kind: three paragraph topics from FDE's closed list; the child writes one

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `topics` = three different titles from closed_lists.paragraphs, exactly as listed. The paper sets no length, so the key awards no mark for length, and the model answer states no sentence count or range (never "three to five supporting sentences"); a content point pays any N relevant ideas, 1 each, up to the marks it carries, and says so.

slots.instruction_en: Develop a story with a moral from the given outline. Also suggest a suitable title.

grain.kind: an outline of 8–12 cues separated by dashes, ending with "Moral"

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = the outline, 8–12 short cues separated by " — ", ending "— Moral". No title. The outline shares the theme or events of the Q2 passage with no other part of the paper: write it about a different place, characters and moral from the Q2 passage (v37: both were a child freeing a hurt bird, kindness, the bird singing next morning).

slots.instruction_en: Describe the picture with the help of the given word bank. Use at least four of the words. Also suggest a suitable title.

grain.kind: a nine-word bank for an everyday scene (classroom, park, market)

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = a one-line scene for the teacher (e.g. "children painting in an art lesson"), `words` = 8–10 words a child would use to describe that scene. The paper prints a frame and the word bank; a picture of the scene prints in the frame (the teacher adds one if it cannot be drawn). Never describe the picture to the child. `describe_en` = a short English description of the scene that names the things behind the words, drawn as a plain black outline picture in the frame; it is never shown to the child. The model answer states only what `describe_en` lists, so `describe_en` says how many of each person or thing there are, where they are, and whether a seat is empty ("two children on the swings, an empty bench beside the slide"), and the answer adds no person, count or place it leaves out (v35: the key put a child on a bench the picture shows empty).

frame.title_en: Picture (pasted or drawn by the teacher)

slots.teacher_note_en: Paste or draw a picture that fits the word bank in the frame before photocopying.

lines_en: MCQs: 1 mark for the letter. Two circles or an overwritten answer = 0.
M = method · A = answer · U = unit · K = key point · L = label.
"Attempt any N": tell children to answer exactly N. If more are answered, mark all and keep the best N.
